text:
Google led the Series B of Bengaluru space-tech startup Pixxel. NVIDIA is now on Sarvam AI's cap table. Big corporates are writing real cheques into Indian startups.

Corporate VCs bring more than money: cloud credits, chips, distribution and a possible future acquirer. Qualcomm alone has backed 40+ Indian companies since 2007, and added a $150M India AI fund this year.

In this carousel: 8 global corporate investors that back Indian founders, from Google's equity-free accelerator and PayPal Ventures to Qualcomm, NVIDIA, Amazon, Hitachi, Visa and MUFG, with stage, cheque, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: a corporate VC invests where its business is going. Before you pitch, show how your product grows their platform, chips or payment volume. Start with their startup programme or a business-unit partnership; the investment often follows.

text:
Lightrock backs DeHaat and WayCool. Acumen has put over $41M into 40 Indian companies. Global impact capital is one of the most overlooked sources of money for Indian founders.

These investors back startups that serve farmers, small businesses, rural customers and the climate, and many write cheques from seed all the way to growth rounds.

In this carousel: 8 global impact and climate investors with recent Indian deals, from Accion Ventures and Acumen to ABC Impact, Lightrock, Circulate Capital, LeapFrog and GEF Capital, with stage, cheque, portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: impact investors want proof of impact as much as revenue. Bring clear numbers, like farmers served, tonnes recycled or first-time borrowers, along with your unit economics. Pitch the fund whose thesis matches your customer.
